idea.title: The first reply wins the client
idea.angle: Buyers message several agents at once; the one who replies first usually gets the viewing
idea.hook: The first reply wins the client.

slides.heading: The first reply **wins** the client.
slides.body: Not the best agent. Not the best listing.

slides.heading: Buyers don't wait
slides.body: A buyer in Accra sends the same DM to several agents. Whoever answers first starts the conversation.

slides.heading: Slow sounds like **no**
slides.body: A reply three hours later reads like you're not interested. By then they're chatting with someone else.

slides.heading: Reply in minutes
slides.body: Even a short holding message beats silence: "Hi! Yes, it's available. Sending details now."

slides.heading: Ask one question
slides.body: "Are you buying or renting, and which area works for you?" Now you're in a conversation.

slides.heading: Offer two times
slides.body: "Can you view on Saturday at 10am or Monday at 4pm?" Don't wait for them to suggest.

caption:
The first reply wins the client.

Buyers don't message one agent. They message several, on WhatsApp and Instagram, at the same time.
The one who answers first gets the conversation. And usually the viewing.
Reply fast, even if it's a short holding message.
Ask one question to get them talking.
Offer two viewing times instead of "when are you free?"

Honest question: how long does a new enquiry usually wait for your first reply? 👇

idea.title: AI isn't smart on its own
idea.angle: Kortexa's core belief: the system and prompting around AI is what makes it work
idea.hook: AI isn't smart on its own.

slides.heading: AI isn't **smart** on its own.
slides.body: It's only as good as the system built around it.

slides.heading: Plug-and-play guesses
slides.body: A generic chatbot doesn't know your listings, prices or areas. So it guesses. Buyers notice.

slides.heading: It can't know
slides.body: "Is the 3-bedroom in East Legon still available?" Without your real listings, any answer is a guess.

slides.heading: Feed it your listings
slides.body: Real prices, locations and availability. Answers come from your data, not guesswork.

slides.heading: Script what it asks
slides.body: Budget, area, timeline. The qualifying questions are designed in, not left to chance.

slides.heading: Hand over at the right time
slides.body: Serious buyer or tricky question? It passes to you, with the details already collected.

caption:
AI isn't smart on its own.

A plug-and-play chatbot doesn't know your listings, your prices or your areas. So it guesses.
A well-built system answers from your own data.
It asks the qualifying questions you'd ask: budget, area, timeline.
And it knows when to step back and hand the buyer to you.
The tool matters less than how it's set up.

idea.title: Reply to 'I'll think about it' without sounding pushy
idea.angle: Two or three short follow-up messages that keep the door open

slides.heading: "I'll think about it." **Now what?**
slides.body: 3 messages that keep the door open without sounding desperate.

slides.heading: Don't chase. **Help.**
slides.body: "Just checking in" gets ignored. Give them a reason to reply instead.

slides.heading: Find the doubt
slides.body: "No pressure at all. What's the one thing you're still unsure about: price, location or timing?"

slides.heading: Bring something new
slides.body: "Hi [Name], a similar 2-bedroom just came up in Spintex, slightly cheaper. Should I send photos?"

slides.heading: The soft close
slides.body: "Hi [Name], should I keep this on your list or close your file for now? Either is fine."

slides.heading: Easy to answer
slides.body: A clear question is easy to reply to. Even "not yet" tells you where you stand.

caption:
"I'll think about it." Now what?

Most agents either chase too hard or go quiet. Both lose the client.
Same day: ask what they're unsure about. Price, location or timing.
Two days later: bring something new, like a similar listing.
One week later: ask if you should keep it on their list or close the file.
Swap in your own listing and area, then copy and send on WhatsApp.

Which one would you send first? 👇

idea.title: Your ad budget isn't the problem. Your reply speed is.
idea.angle: Paying for ads that bring leads nobody answers fast enough
idea.hook: It's not your ads. It's your replies.

slides.heading: It's not your ads. It's your **replies.**
slides.body: You're paying for leads nobody answers fast enough.

slides.heading: You paid for that DM
slides.body: Every enquiry from your Instagram ad cost you cedis or naira. Leave it for hours and that money is gone.

slides.heading: Your real **cost**
slides.body: Ad spend ÷ enquiries = cost per lead. Now count how many got a reply within an hour.

slides.heading: Check last week
slides.body: Scroll back through your DMs. How long did each enquiry wait for your first reply?

slides.heading: Find the gaps
slides.body: Evenings, weekends, viewing days. That's when ad leads sit unanswered.

slides.heading: Fix speed, then spend
slides.body: A bigger budget with slow replies just means more unanswered DMs.

caption:
It's not your ads. It's your replies.

Every DM from your ad cost you money.
If it waits hours for a reply, the buyer has already moved on.
Work out your cost per lead: ad spend divided by enquiries.
Then check how many of those enquiries got a reply within the hour.
Fix reply speed before you raise the budget.

When do most of your ad leads arrive: daytime, evenings or weekends? 👇
